svg.title: 3. Noisy-neighbour controls, layer by layer
svg.text: Noisy neighbours: every shared layer gets its own per-tenant limit, so one tenant's spike slows that tenant, not the platform
Fair queues keep dwell time low
1. Limits come from the tier config, not from code. Changing a tier is a config push.
2. The tenant id used for limits comes from the authorizer, never from a header
the client sets. Otherwise one tenant can spend another tenant's budget.
3. A big tenant is allowed to be slower. It is never allowed to make others slower.
4. Bulk and interactive work never share a queue or a worker pool.
5. If one tenant is consistently above 25% of a shared resource, that is a
sales conversation about a bigger tier or a silo, not an ops ticket.
